land.text: the northern provinces and the Flemish and Brabantine towns that signed the Union in 1579-1580, taken out of the Habsburg Netherlands then ruled for Philip II

predecessors.note: No dossier exists yet for the Habsburg (Spanish) Netherlands; its Cliopatria row is missing. The slug is the one this batch uses for it.

land.text: the Union's land, now the independent United Provinces after the Act of Abjuration of 26 July 1581; Cliopatria's Dutch Republic row starts in 1582

successors.note: The Union page calls the Union the foundation of the Dutch Republic. Cliopatria keeps two rows, so this dossier ends in July 1581 and dutch-republic starts in 1582.

capitals.name: Antwerp
capitals.note: The page says Antwerp was the union's capital until it fell to the Spanish (it gives no year; the Eighty Years' War page dates the fall of Antwerp to 1585). The page describes the Union as an alliance based on an agreement.

correction.text: The Union at the end of 1579: Cliopatria's full shape without Overijssel and Drenthe (joined April 1580) and without Bruges and Lier (joined February 1580); it holds Holland, Zeeland, Utrecht, Groningen, Friesland and the Guelders quarters, plus Ghent, Ypres, Antwerp, Breda, Brussels and Amersfoort, who joined in 1579

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria draws one constant shape for 1579-1581, which is the membership reached in April 1580. The page dates the joins: 23 January 1579 Holland, Zeeland, Utrecht, Groningen province; later in 1579 Ghent, Friesland's cities, three Guelders quarters, Amersfoort, Ypres, Antwerp, Breda, Brussels; February 1580 Lier and Bruges; April 1580 Overijssel and Drenthe.

correction.text: The full Union of 1580-1581 (holds 1580-1581; 1579 is the keyframe above): Cliopatria's shape clipped to 300 km of the Low Countries, which drops the one cell at Orange (44.2 N), a place that is not among the members the page lists

keyframe_review.note: 38,590 km2; the page gives no area. The shape reaches Overijssel and Drenthe (joined April 1580), Bruges and Lier (February 1580), Ghent, Antwerp and Brussels, matching the members the page lists. The page also lists Tournai and Valenciennes as members: Cliopatria has no cell there (Hainaut 0 per cell count), a gap of two cities. The Orange cell (Principality of Orange, ruled by William of Nassau) was not a member.

region.text: Holland, Zeeland, Utrecht (but not all of it), and the province (not the city) of Groningen

ledger.note: 1579: Holland, Zeeland, Utrecht and the province of Groningen sign the Union of Utrecht on 23 January, in reaction to the Union of Arras. 'The treaty was signed on 23 January by' Holland, Zeeland, Utrecht (but not all of it), and the province (not the city) of Groningen; 'The treaty was a reaction of the Protestant provinces to the 1579 Union of Arras'. The page gives no place for the signing.

region.text: Ghent, cities of Friesland, three Guelders quarters (Nijmegen, Veluwe, Zutphen), Amersfoort (summer 1579), Ypres, Antwerp, Breda, and Brussels (summer 1579); Upper Guelders never signed

ledger.note: 1579: Ghent, Antwerp, Brussels and the Guelders quarters join the Union (month 6 stands for 'summer 1579' and keeps the ledger in order; the page dates only some joins to the summer and the rest to 'later in 1579'). The page lists as joining later in 1579: Ghent, cities of Friesland, three Guelders quarters (Nijmegen, Veluwe, Zutphen), Amersfoort (summer 1579), Ypres, Antwerp, Breda, and Brussels (summer 1579). Friesland and Gelderland are drawn whole as the Cliopatria shape does; Upper Guelders never signed.

region.text: Lier and Bruges, plus surrounding areas; the city of Groningen also signed after shifting its position

ledger.note: February 1580: Bruges and Lier join. The page lists as joining in February 1580: Lier and Bruges, plus surrounding areas; the city of Groningen also signed after shifting its position. The page does not date the city of Groningen's signature separately.
April 1580: Overijssel and Drenthe join, completing the Union's northern membership. The page lists Overijssel and Drenthe as joining in April 1580.

region.text: the Union's whole land, which becomes the independent United Provinces

ledger.note: 26 July 1581: the Act of Abjuration, 'a de facto declaration of independence from Spain', turns the rebel Union into the independent United Provinces (the Dutch Republic of Cliopatria from 1582). The Union page agrees on the year: in 1581 the United Provinces declared independence from the king in the Act of Abjuration.

wars.name: Eighty Years' War

zones.text: Flanders and Brabant, which the Union held in 1579-1581 and which Parma then reconquered (the page says Flanders was almost entirely conquered by Spanish troops, as was half of Brabant)

wars.outcome: The Union of 1579 was the northern provinces' alliance against Spain; they declared independence in 1581 and Spain recognised the Dutch Republic by the Peace of Münster (30 January 1648).
wars.note: Infobox dates 'c. 1566/1568 - 30 January 1648'. Within this dossier's life the pages date no campaign: Parma's reconquests and the fall of Antwerp (1585) come after the Union dossier ends and are in dutch-republic. The war ran c. 1566/1568 to 30 January 1648 (Eighty Years' War infobox); from and to are clipped to the Union's life (1579-1581) by reviewer eu-09-j (brief rule: wars inside the life).

certainty.note: A war-time alliance of provinces and towns: membership is by signature and changes month by month (January 1579, summer 1579, February and April 1580), and the front with the Spanish-held south is not a surveyed line.

sources.title: Union of Utrecht
sources.note: Signatories and joining dates (23 January 1579, summer 1579, February and April 1580), the Union of Arras, Antwerp as capital, 'foundation of the Dutch Republic', member list; no area; no date for the fall of Flanders and Brabant.

notes: Written by eu-09-j on 2026-10-25 from two pages (budget 1-2). TYPE: the Union is typed rebel (the northern provinces against the king of Spain, 1579 to the Act of Abjuration of 1581, after which the Dutch Republic carries the same land as an independent state); a reviewer who prefers state may retype it, nothing else changes. The Orange cell: Cliopatria's shape contains one cell at Orange in Provence (44.2 N), as does every Dutch Republic shape to 1795; the Union page's member list does not include it, so the correction clips to 300 km of the Low Countries. The Principality of Orange page (opened for dutch-republic) shows it as a sovereign principality inside the Empire under William of Nassau. MEMBERS LACKING A CELL: the page lists Tournai and Valenciennes among the members, Cliopatria has none. The shape's 8 cells outside the Netherlands and Belgium are three German cells beside Overijssel and Drenthe and four estuary or coastal cells (they stay in the clipped shape). COUNTERPARTS: habsburg-netherlands (the Habsburg or Spanish Netherlands, 1482-1795) has no Cliopatria row and no dossier; every gain here names it. Gazetteer names not in places.jsonl: Ypres, Breda, Lier, Amersfoort. Spanish reconquest of Flanders and Brabant is undated on both pages (1584-1585 for Ghent, Bruges, Brussels and Antwerp is known only for Antwerp, 1585, from the Eighty Years' War page); it falls after the Union dossier ends and is recorded in dutch-republic (1585 loss).
